description: Phase distortion oscillator — four waveforms at once, each drawn against a phase curve you bend by hand or by voltage

params.text: Sets the pitch in semitones, 0 giving C4 at 261.63Hz
Trims the pitch a semitone either way
Switches the oscillator between a clean digital engine and an analogue one with drift and softer edges
Switches the sync input between hard sync, which restarts the cycle outright, and soft sync, which reverses it instead
Sets how deeply the FM jack moves the frequency, from none to full

inputs.text: Pitch at a volt per octave, added to the frequency knob
A rising edge here syncs the oscillator
0V to 10V sets how far along the cycle the bend in the phase curve falls, replacing the point dragged on the display
0V to 10V sets how high the bend in the phase curve is taken, replacing the point dragged on the display
Modulates the frequency, scaled by the FM knob

outputs.text: The sine wave, drawn against the bent phase curve
The triangle wave, drawn against the bent phase curve
The saw wave, drawn against the bent phase curve
The square wave, drawn against the bent phase curve

notes: drag the point on the display to bend the phase curve; a straight curve gives the plain waveforms, and speeding the phase up in one part of the cycle and slowing it in another reshapes them
menu: Mode: — switches between OSC and LFO, LFO dividing the frequency by 100
